abstract: Accurate and scalable visual document retrieval (VDR) requires both fine-grained page understanding and efficient indexing, yet existing approaches struggle to achieve both. OCR-based text retrieval adds preprocessing latency and can lose visual and structural cues needed to understand complex pages. Single-vector vision-language models bypass OCR, but compressing an entire page into one vector limits the granularity of query--document matching. Multi-vector retrievers with MaxSim provide finer interactions, yet demand large indexes and still leave room for accuracy improvements. We argue that overcoming these limitations requires preserving query-relevant page evidence throughout representation learning and index construction. To this end, we introduce \textbf{\textit{EVIE}} (Evidence-Vector-Informed Embeddings), a family of native visual document retrievers integrating three key innovations: (1) Evidence-judged data governance, which uses a multimodal judge to identify answer-bearing positives and filter unreliable negatives. (2) Bidirectional teacher--student learning with symmetric listwise distillation and prefix-based Matryoshka representation learning (Prefix-MRL), enabling one student checkpoint to serve six nested embedding dimensions without re-encoding. (3) Hierarchical agglomerative index compression (HAC), which clusters page tokens with spatial regularization and stores semantic centroids for single-stage MaxSim retrieval. Extensive experiments across 138 tasks from ViDoRe V1, V2, V3, and JinaVDR validate EVIE. EVIE-8B achieves 66.75 nDCG@10 on V3, exceeding the best external baseline by 1.43 points, with a four-suite average of 79.51. EVIE-4.5B with HAC retains 59.58 nDCG@10 at only 3.81 GiB per million pages, reducing vector payload by $128\times$. Together, these results improve the accuracy--storage trade-off for visual document retrieval.

abstract: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. Existing datasets also cover a limited range of games, often without explicit tasks or verifiable outcomes. To address these gaps, we introduce Game2Player, a framework that co-develops game environments and players to collect diverse and verifiable gameplay experience at scale. In the Game2Player loop, a Builder agent adapts existing web games, exposes their internal state, and defines tasks with state-based progress measures and success checks. A Coding Player and a VLM Player then attempt the tasks and report problems to the Builder for repair, so that play serves as both environment validation and training data collection. With Game2Player, we build 568 verified web games with 3,436 tasks, collect 15.7K trajectories (307 hours of gameplay), and hold out 50 games as the benchmark PlayerBench. To evaluate the collected experience as training data, we train VLM agents with progress-weighted SFT, assigning greater weight to steps that advance task progress. Game2Player-9B improves progress from 14.3% to 31.2% on PlayerBench and from 30.0% to 53.1% on the external GameWorld benchmark. More broadly, our work suggests a path for visual agents to scale their gameplay experience by building, verifying, and learning from existing game worlds.

abstract: We examine whether post-origin training information inflates the measured accuracy and economic value of financial forecasts. We evaluate five sets of financial time-series foundation models, each comprising independently trained annual vintages under U.S., global, and factor-augmented training environments, across 14 equity markets and four forecast horizons. Rolling comparisons vary the annual vintage for a fixed forecast; fixed-vintage comparisons hold the vintage fixed as target windows move across its training cutoff. Each alternative forecast is paired with an origin-aligned point-in-time (PIT) benchmark using identical numerical histories and inference protocols. In the U.S.-trained reference environment, post-origin vintages materially revise informative PIT forecasts but generally reduce accuracy in both designs. Pooled rolling comparisons yield higher mean squared forecast errors in 18 of 20 U.S. model-set-horizon combinations. The origin-crossing update also performs worse on average than an equally long pre-origin update. Under a common constrained allocation rule using one-month forecasts, median exposed-minus-PIT differences in annualized certainty-equivalent returns are -1.77 percentage points in the United States and -2.14 points internationally. Global and factor-augmented training produce more mixed predictive effects. An exact squared-error decomposition shows that revisions improve accuracy when their error-correcting benefit exceeds their mean squared magnitude; under U.S. training, alignment with PIT errors generally falls short of this requirement. Temporal exposure therefore establishes an information-set violation, not sufficient evidence of inflated predictive accuracy or investor value.

abstract: This paper focuses on tightly coupled antenna (TCA) array systems with high mutual coupling, resulting in wideband signals. We analyze the target detection capability of such systems with joint time and frequency approaches. We assume a target whose echo signals are unknown wideband signals and show the opportunity that TCAs create in target detection. We consider temporal and spectral dynamics of the signal as either constant, slowly or rapidly varying in frequency and time, giving nine possible cases in total. For each case we derive a detector and present thorough analysis for the distribution of the detector test statistic, considering frequency-dependent noise correlation due to mutual coupling. For the cases with a signal changing slowly in at least one domain we propose a novel detection approach based on estimation of the signal via local averaging of the samples. We also derive a detector that results in an upper bound on detection performance for comparison. We compare our analytical results with simulations, showing perfect accuracy of our derived distributions. In addition, we assess the performance of the detectors under various time/frequency variation rates. We show the superior performance of our proposed detection approach in comparison to other detectors including an extended energy detector we derive for correlated noise as well as both frequency and time samples.

abstract: Abstract Personal AI agents now persist: they hold accounts, mailboxes, long-term memory, and open-ended task streams, yet the dominant way to improve them remains capability-side: prompt engineering, larger models, longer thinking, and retrieval. We argue that long-lived agents are missing an incentive layer. We formalize an incentive not as text in a prompt but as a runtime contract over the agent's operating point (model tier, test-time compute, memory budget, tool authority, task priority, verification, and compensation) that the agent's policy must causally consume. We develop a principal-agent model with hidden effort, a contractible operating point, and costly verification. We derive (i) a non-consumption invariance principle separating genuine incentives from prompt-level persuasion, (ii) a persistence-as-discount theorem making identity continuity a precondition for sustained effort, (iii) an incentive-capability exchange-rate frontier yielding a per-task routing rule, and (iv) a Goodhart bound for multi-channel verification, plus a three-channel decomposition of mechanism gains (allocation, verification, continuation). A 240-run real-LLM experiment with two models and 60 verifiable tasks shows that prompt-level incentive framing has no detectable effect (p = 0.62), whereas runtime allocation raises success on the hardest task family from 0.60 to 1.00 (p = 0.008) at 4.8x price-weighted cost; the exchange-rate theorem predicts the break-even baseline at 0.21. A 20-seed, 3,000-task simulation shows resource ROI rising from 7.09 to 16.67 and gaming falling from 0.333 to 0.115. Code, simulator, and all results are released; live deployment remains future work.

abstract: This paper introduces "BladeSEI", a multi-channel receiver, multi-day dataset of radar pulses recorded over-the-air from 12 Software Defined Radios (SDRs) for the purpose of Specific Emitter Identification (SEI). The aim of this dataset is to enable investigation into robust SEI techniques that are able to generalise across different receiver channels and recording sessions. The dataset consists of two waveform types per emitter, a 50 microsecond chirped pulse of 40 MHz bandwidth and a 10 microsecond unmodulated pulse. Pulses are captured simultaneously on four synchronised analogue-to-digital converter (ADC) channels of a multi-channel receiver over three recording sessions on two days: a baseline session, an identical repeat on the following day, and a session in which the emitters were thermally conditioned to alter their operating temperature. Initial results using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Inception and ResNet based classifiers, trained and tested on a single ADC channel and recording session, show that the BladeRF emitters can be discriminated at high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), with ResNet achieving a macro-F1 above 0.98 at 25 dB for both waveforms, and performance degrading towards random guessing at 0 dB.

abstract: Beamforming designs for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in cell-free multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems face the challenge to stay reliable under uncertainties from both channel state information (CSI) as well as clutter. To this end, this paper proposes an impairment-aware heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN) framework for beamforming that obtains the CSI error level and the clutter covariance as edge features, which enables a single trained model to adapt to both impairments. In particular, the GNN is trained on a low quantile of the minimum user rate with a clutter-aware signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio, balanced by a normalized Tchebycheff scalarization. Simulation results show that the proposed GNN framework outperforms the considered baselines in sensing-only and communication-only settings. Depending on the operating point, a single GNN model attains approximately 97\% of each baseline's rate while serving both functionalities at once. The model further generalizes to unseen CSI error levels and clutter counts and renders the ISAC system resilient.

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) enable rich semantic user profiles for recommendation, but such profiles are more expensive to generate and are not necessarily desirable to deploy uniformly. We study whether LLM-generated profiles can instead be invoked selectively within a production recommendation pipeline. Using a real-world streaming dataset covering movies, TV shows, and sports content, we train a serving-time routing gate that assigns each user to either a collaborative sequential recommendation model or a recommendation model driven by an LLM-generated profile. The gate uses only serving-time features and learns to identify users for whom profile-based routing can increase Novelty@10 while preserving ranking relevance. A routing threshold controls how aggressively users are sent to the generative model, exposing a tunable novelty--relevance trade-off. At an overall NDCG-loss budget of 5\%, the learned gate increases Novelty@10 by 6.5\% while routing 12.5\% of users, outperforming simple heuristic and random routing policies at comparable relevance cost. These results show that LLM-generated user profiles can serve as a controllable complement to collaborative recommendation, while results with non-generative semantic profiles indicate that the benefit stems from selective routing rather than LLM generation alone.

abstract: We propose an electromagnetic wireless channel model for accurate target localization in radar-like sensing scenarios. The model employs a self-consistent method grounded in wave scattering theory and imposing boundary conditions, providing the (impedance) channel transfer matrix for a propagation channel with a single target modeled as a cylindrical scatterer. The model is: i) physics-based, as it includes electromagnetic interactions between objects; ii) unified, as it is valid in both near-and far-field regions. Within the canonical two-dimensional and 2.5-dimensional configurations with line-source and dipole-source excitations, respectively, the model supports dielectric cylinders with frequency-dependent permittivity. Localization accuracy is assessed via the Cramér–Rao lower bound for a dielectric cylinder with variable position, radius, and dielectric constant. Provisions for future extensions to extended targets are discussed in the context of 3GPP channel modeling.

abstract: This paper introduces "RadarML", a publicly available dataset of modulated radar pulses recorded over-the-air across multiple semi-independent receiver channels. The dataset was generated using the UCL ARESTOR platform which is a Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC) based Software Defined Radio (SDR). The dataset contains a library of around two million waveforms with varying centre frequencies, bandwidths, pulse widths and modulations, with 1,000 examples of each signal variation per receiver channel. The goal of this dataset is to enable comparative analysis of radar modulation classification techniques on real data and stimulate research into multi-channel signal detection and modulation classification methods.

abstract: Various applications require accurate 3-D characterization of magnetic fields with high spatial and temporal resolution. Building on our previously introduced spherical magnetic field camera employing 86 three-axis Hall sensors arranged on a spherical surface, we present a novel magnetic-field reconstruction approach based on the magnetic scalar potential and its spherical harmonic expansion. Unlike the previous reconstruction method that expands each vector component separately, our scalar-potential-based formulation is inherently consistent with Maxwell's equations for source-free fields by design, yielding curl-free and divergence-free field models. Using a simulated magnetic gradient field generated by two permanent magnets, we demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher reconstruction accuracy, improved robustness to sensor noise and failure, and substantially reduced non-physical divergence and curl compared to the component-wise baseline. Furthermore, the scalar-potential approach attains superior performance with fewer coefficients, indicating a more efficient use of measurement data allowing higher-degree polynomial representations.

abstract: Can a regulator promise both a risk ceiling and a development deadline when safety productivity is unknown? A ceiling below the final model's unprotected hazard requires a minimum stock of safety knowledge, so both promises hold only if weak research can be ruled out. Learning first and then replaying development, with spare compute in safety, needs productivity 21 percent above that lower bound, or 3.3 percent with state risk alone. The policy holds catastrophe risk to 8 percent, against 75 under full speed, and costs customers 13 percent of five-year services. Rules that fix compute allocation fix dates, not risk.

abstract: Purpose: Patient-specific electro-anatomical models (EAMs) of the implanted cochlea are crucial for auditory nerve fiber simulation in cochlear implant (CI) programming and neural health estimation. Fitting an EAM to the stimulation current induced non-stimulating electrode voltage (SCINSEV) currently requires manual expert adjustment or exhaustive search over precomputed forward solutions, neither of which scales to routine clinical use. We present an automated optimization pipeline that fits patient specific EAMs in minutes. abstract: Population aging and fertility decline are occurring simultaneously worldwide, straining labor supply and pension systems. China began a gradual delayedretirement (GDR) reform in 2025, raising statutory retirement ages on different schedules for men, female cadres, and female workers across birth cohorts. To evaluate its effects on older individuals and within the family, we develop a model of older adults' retirement, intergenerational transfers, and adult children's fertility decisions, with parameters estimated via fuzzy regression discontinuity at the pre-2025 statutory retirement ages. Counterfactual simulations show that, for mature reform cohorts, the GDR reform increases older employment and monetary transfers to adult children but reduces grandparental childcare. Because the reduction in childcare outweighs the increase in monetary transfers, fertility and older adults' welfare decline, with particularly large losses among lower-income women. Fully flexible retirement, mandatory partial retirement, and mandatory full-time work do not raise employment without similarly reducing fertility and welfare. Childcare subsidies can offset the declines in fertility and welfare, while restricting eligibility to women or lower-income women requires higher subsidy rates but reduces average fiscal expenditure. These findings suggest that evaluations of retirement policy should consider not only its direct effects on older adults' labor supply, but also its fertility effects through intergenerational transfers; childcare support can help mitigate these negative intergenerational effects of delayed retirement.

abstract: Deep-learning-based radar target detectors can achieve strong performance in complex sensing environments. However, in time-varying environments, changes in clutter characteristics may cause the distribution of echoes to deviate from that of the training data, thereby degrading detector reliability. Timely identification of such degradation requires an accurate assessment of the deployed detector's performance; however, ground-truth labels for radar echoes are typically unavailable during deployment. This paper investigates label-free performance estimation for deployed deep learning-based radar target detectors. We first show that confidence-based estimators tend to overestimate detection performance under distribution shift because they fail to account for the discrepancy between the detector-induced pseudo-label distribution and the true label distribution. To address this limitation, we propose probabilistic optimal transport (POT), which assesses deployment performance by computing the Wasserstein distance between the detector's output probability distribution on unlabeled deployment echoes and the label distribution in the training data. We further develop thresholded probabilistic optimal transport (TPOT), which suppresses the influence of anomalous transport costs on the Wasserstein-distance-based estimate, thereby improving estimation robustness. Experiments on a publicly measured radar dataset demonstrate that POT and TPOT consistently outperform representative label-free baselines across deployment scenarios with varying degrees of data distribution shift.

abstract: Economic analysis of effective policies for managing epidemics requires an integrated economic and epidemiological approach. We develop and estimate a spatial, micro-founded model of the joint evolution of economic variables and the spread of an epidemic. We empirically discipline the model using new U.S. county-level data on health, mobility, employment outcomes, and non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) at a daily frequency. Absent policy or medical interventions, the model predicts an initial period of exponential growth in new cases, followed by a protracted period of roughly constant case levels and reduced economic activity. Nevertheless, if vaccine development proved impossible, and suppression cannot entirely eradicate the disease, a utilitarian policymaker cannot improve significantly over the laissez-faire equilibrium by using lockdowns. Conversely, if a vaccine will arrive within two years, NPIs can improve upon the laissez-faire outcome by dramatically decreasing the number of infectious agents and keeping infections low until vaccine arrival. Mitigation measures that reduce viral transmission (e.g., mask-wearing) both reduce the virus's spread and increase economic activity.

abstract: Generative AI makes a paradox newly visible: learning from a common source can improve what each firm does today while narrowing the variety available for tomorrow's discoveries. The tension extends beyond AI. Fields turn recurring features of successful organizations into portable practices-just-in-time production, freemium business models, or mixture-of-experts architectures. These collective abstractions are partial templates others can adapt, not designs or universal prescriptions. We study how they shape discovery in a model of firms searching interdependent landscapes. A collective repertoire extracts practices from patterns shared by leading configurations; firms vary in how they evaluate those practices locally. The model reveals a generativity chain: population diversity supplies heterogeneous experience, collective abstraction turns it into reusable options, and situated judgment matches options to local needs. Collective learning is not inherently homogenizing. Copying leaders consumes diversity quickly, whereas repertoires paired with local judgment preserve generative capacity. Environmental disruption exposes the consequences: it devalues accumulated knowledge but reopens local search, helping homogeneous, exhausted industries while harming diverse industries whose repertoire remains useful-even though diverse industries still perform better overall. Recurring practices may also outlive their usefulness, making popularity a poor test of validity after change. These findings matter for organizations using generative AI, best-practice communities, and research fields converging on dominant strands. Generativity requires governing the diversity feeding knowledge and the judgment applied to it. Learning systems should be judged not only by the answers they spread today, but by whether they preserve the differences from which tomorrow's answers can be made.

abstract: Nonstationarity and heterogeneous dynamics are common in financial and macroeconomic time series. Volatility alternates between calm and turbulent regimes, interest rates follow monetary-policy cycles, and major events trigger persistent structural shifts. We propose the Time-partitioning Gaussian Process Mixture Model (TPGPMM), a Bayesian nonparametric framework for regime identification and nonstationary prediction that infers such regimes and their within-regime dependence from data, without Markovian assumptions. It combines (i) an adaptive Pitman-Yor process prior on ordered compositions, mapped to block lengths with contiguity enforced by construction, and (ii) regime-specific Gaussian processes for temporal dependence, yielding a nonstationary predictive distribution. By inferring its discount parameter, the prior adapts to homogeneous and highly heterogeneous regime lengths. Unlike sequential or Markov-switching methods, it flags persistent structural shifts as change points rather than reacting to transient shocks. A split-merge Metropolis-within-Gibbs sampler with exact Gibbs updates of regime boundaries jointly learns change points and hyperparameters in batch, quantifying uncertainty over the partition and within-regime dynamics. With an RBF kernel and a fixed, data-informed noise level, TPGPMM produces a sparse, confident segmentation. On simulated data it recovers the true regimes, and on the CBOE Volatility Index and the 10-year US Treasury yield it identifies regimes aligned with documented market and monetary-policy events. For prediction, variants estimating the noise level fit better than change-point baselines and fit and forecast better than the main specification, at the cost of a less sparse or less event-aligned segmentation; with a regime mean, they fit better than a fitted stationary Gaussian process and have lower forecast RMSE except at the shortest horizons.

abstract: UI grounding asks a model to find the screen element that a user instruction refers to. Most current systems use a vision-language model (VLM) that reads a screenshot and outputs pixel coordinates. We study this task on Urdu mobile web pages, a setting with no published UI grounding results. Instead of regressing coordinates, we take the candidate elements from the page DOM and train a 279M-parameter cross-encoder (mDeBERTa-v3-base) to pick one. The click point is the centre of the picked element's box, so it is exact whenever the right element is picked. We built a frozen test set of 304 instructions from six Urdu news sites; 149 of them (49%) are referential and never quote the full target text. Test domains were banned from training data before collection started. The ranker scores 73.4% point-in-box accuracy, against 29.6% for UI-TARS-2B and 23.7% for Qwen2.5-VL-7B, both zero-shot. On the referential slice the ranker scores 65.8%, against 30.2% for a string-matching baseline that needs no training. In a controlled comparison at small scale, with training data drawn from the same pages, a coordinate-regression model of similar size scores 1.6%. Adding element geometry as input tokens gives the best variant, at 75.7%. The ranker's errors concentrate in two places: elements that share identical text, and ordinal instructions such as "the fourth link".

abstract: Does a widening gap between company revenue and staff expense per employee provide evidence of declining rent-sharing? We examine how reporting selection and sector composition affect that inference, as a follow-up to Acemoglu, He, and le Maire's Eclipse of Rent-Sharing. We assemble 7,000 company-years for 695 firms over 2015-2025. In a fixed sample of 75 staffexpense reporters, nominal revenue per employee rises 83.6%, while staff expense per employee rises 51.0%. The pooled expense-to-revenue ratio falls, but the pattern is concentrated in financial firms; among the other 25 reporters, aggregate staff expense per employee grows slightly faster than aggregate revenue per employee. These accounting measures identify neither real productivity nor the allocation of its gains between labor and capital. A separate audit of the original paper's reported estimates finds that some US output effects remain imprecisely estimated, while several Danish estimates support tighter bounds. The fitted reporting-probability model exhibits concentrated weights, substantial two-group imbalance and sectors without reporters; it does not justify generalizing payroll results. We extend the original study's measurement discussion to public-company accounts and qualify a blanket interpretation of no output effects: precision varies across its estimates. Our sector-dependent accounting results neither confirm nor overturn its causal wage and labor-share findings.

abstract: Developing countries have increased sanitation investment to improve child health. However, scaling up latrine construction can cause water pollution externalities owing to insufficient infrastructure for the treatment of fecal sludge, offsetting the direct health benefits. I estimate the negative externalities of an Indian sanitation policy that subsidized the construction of over 100 million latrines. Exploiting geographical variations in soil characteristics that affect the feasibility of latrine construction, I find that this policy increases fecal contamination of rivers by 72%. Although the policy reduces diarrheal child mortality overall, this positive health effect is eliminated when upstream areas lack adequate wastewater infrastructure.

abstract: When can shocks affecting households in a few counties, such as income or wealth losses from storms, move credit prices? I develop a propagation operator that traces their effects through social ties and weights each county's response by how strongly it changes desired bond demand. Holding intermediary capital fixed, this weighted response determines the household-demand component of the excess bond premium. Given known measurement relationships and independently measured demand sensitivities, household measurements recover it exactly when they capture the combination that changes bond demand for the shocks and horizons studied, without reconstructing the entire propagation system. As responses decay at different rates across network patterns and channels, a location's financial importance generically changes with the horizon, so no fixed centrality measure summarizes it. Empirically, social exposure to stormdamaged counties is associated with lower spending weeks later outside recorded footprints, net of own weather and competing exposures. Simulations on the observed network turn the recovered response into credit-premium predictions for held-out storms, with demand sensitivities and price impact supplied or estimated from simulated data.

abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the statistical behaviour of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with constant step size under the framework of iterated random functions. Compared with previous studies establishing the convergence of SGD in probability measure, e.g. Wasserstein distance, our approach directly provides the convergence in Euclidean distance by showing the geometric moment contraction of SGD. This new convergence can address the nonstationarity of SGD due to fixed initial points and can provide more refined asymptotics of SGD. Specifically, we prove quenched central limit theorem, invariance principle and α-stable convergence for averaged SGD (ASGD) regardless of initialization. Furthermore, we provide a novel perspective to understand the impact of step sizes in SGD by studying its derivative with respect to the step size. The existence of stationary solutions for the derivative processes is shown, enabling the use of interpolation to recover the full-trajectory of SGD. Subsequently, we utilize multiple step sizes and show an enhanced Richardson–Romberg extrapolation with improved bias representation, which brings ASGD estimates closer to the global optimum. Finally, we propose an online inference method and a bias-reduced variant for the extrapolated ASGD. Empirical confidence intervals are constructed and the coverage probabilities approach the nominal level as n grows.

abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot’s physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

abstract: Rendered images are cheap to label, but a microcontroller classifier must survive 8-bit integer (INT8) quantisation and compute correctly on the chip. Five models, from MobileNetV2 at 224 px to a 61K-parameter convolutional neural network (CNN), were fine-tuned on a six-class scene dataset with and without a synthetic stage, against thresholds fixed in advance, and deployed on an ESP32-S3 and an RP2040. With full real data the stage gave no detectable gain. For the main deployable model the INT8 difference was +0.312 percentage points (pp), its interval below the +1.6 pp gain recomputed from the source study; quantisation did not detectably change it, nor did model size. With 10% of the real data the stage paid off for the CNN, by +3.438 pp on one seed and +2.715 pp over three; its cause is open. On the ESP32-S3 the main model took 152.7 ms and 16.3 mJ above idle per inference, and adding the stage changed neither beyond preset bounds. The model's INT8 outputs matched TensorFlow Lite's reference kernels exactly, but only after a memory overrun in a vendor kernel was patched. On the RP2040 the same model took 1.80 s and 27.3 mJ above idle, about twelve times slower, and the largest 96 px model exceeded the board's flash-capacity limit. Neither the RP2040 nor the host interpreter used for scoring reproduced the reference arithmetic. A synthetic stage is worth adding only when real data are scarce, and on-device INT8 outputs should be checked against reference kernels, not inferred from host scores.

abstract: Abstract Self-supervised pretraining has transformed language and vision, but its value for molecular graph neural networks remains contested; we ask whether pretraining on a large unlabelled corpus improves downstream molecular property prediction. To answer it we adapt LeJEPA - a predictor-free joint-embedding predictive architecture whose embeddings are regularised by Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularisation (SIGReg) - to molecular graphs, and evaluate it with two encoder backbones (a GPS graph transformer and a Chemprop-style D-MPNN) on the Wong et al.\ \cite{Wong2024} antibiotic-activity dataset and the \texttt{ogbg-molhiv} benchmark under a rigorous multi-seed, bootstrap-based protocol. We find that the benefit of pretraining is real at the level of the learned representation but does not robustly survive finetuning. A frozen probe on the pretrained embedding far exceeds the same architecture at random initialisation on both tasks (on \texttt{ogbg-molhiv}, ROC-AUC $0.788$ vs $0.665$, a $+0.123$ lift reaching the published self-supervised band), yet this edge does not convert into a downstream finetuning gain. On the antibiotic scaffold split it is significant on a single canonical partition ($\Delta\text{AUPRC} = +0.041$, $p = 0.010$) but vanishes when replicated across five partitions (pooled $+0.013$, $p = 0.095$), and finetuning is null on the random split, on \texttt{ogbg-molhiv}, and with the D-MPNN backbone. The representational edge is nonetheless real and recoverable by other means. A width-controlled analysis shows the embedding saturates at ${\sim}16$--$32$ effective dimensions while the fingerprint keeps improving to $1024$ bits, and that at matched dimensionality which representation wins depends on the split: the fingerprint leads on validation ($0.799$ vs $0.782$ at $128$ dimensions) and trails on the shifted test scaffolds ($0.759$ vs $0.788$), which the embedding crosses with essentially no loss against the fingerprint's $0.040$. abstract: Abstract A small labelled dataset is memorized long before the training budget runs out, and the one-hot labels that remain to be fitted then mostly sharpen confidence. Model annealing spends the rest of the budget on review and consolidation, relearning from the network's own knowledge. Training is divided into episodes whose learning rate is raised again and cooled, every cooled state joins a memory of past selves, and each new episode learns from the labels, from the tempered predictions of this memory, and from adversarial dreams sought where student and memory disagree most. The memory averages predictions rather than weights, and the deployed network is the last student, so inference costs nothing extra. Across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet and Imagewoof, four architecture families and 5\% to 100\% of the labels, model annealing raises the top-1 accuracy of the AdamW-trained ConvNeXt, ViT and MLP-Mixer over cross-entropy training in 28 of 33 configurations, by 1.3 points on average, and is on par in accuracy with snapshot distillation, the closest competitor. On these families it is better than both in likelihood, calibration and robustness to corruptions and small adversarial perturbations. For an SGD-trained ResNet-18 it lowers accuracy but still improves robustness to small adversarial perturbations. Separating the reheated schedule from relearning shows that relearning helps every family and that the losses come from reheats, which undo most of this network's fit to its training set. How early the accuracy of a cross-entropy run saturates largely separates the AdamW families from ResNet-18 but does not predict the gain within them. With little data, relearning from the latest snapshot without dreams, as snapshot distillation does, compounds overconfidence in the AdamW families from episode to episode. The memory and the dreams each curb most of this drift, and together they remove it.

abstract: Nepali speakers regularly mix English words into conversation, but multilingual speech recognisers often struggle with language switches and the writing script used for English words. We study how to adapt SraVaani, a 449M-parameter hybrid TDT-CTC model, using a 172.8-hour corpus covering six Nepali speech domains. Its pretrained tokenizer does not support digits and several common symbols. Rather than replace it or discard these recordings, we generate Nepali and English readings for numbers and use zero-shot ASR output to select a plausible form. Full fine-tuning reduces test word error rate (WER) from 48.6% to 17.1%; a 12-epoch run reaches 16.3%, compared with 16.4% for fine-tuned Whisper large-v3-turbo. Freezing the encoder increases WER to 25.5%, while excluding numeric clips raises WER on numeric test speech from 14.3% to 21.3%. We also evaluate on FLEURS using both its original references and mixed-script alternatives. The comparison shows that transcription conventions explain part, but not all, of the out-of-domain performance loss.

abstract: We provide an introduction to real-world asset (RWA) tokenization, and develop two economic models connecting this emerging market to classical financial theory. In search for a theory of RWA tokenization, we classify RWA tokenization according to the role of the underlying asset, distinguishing standard RWA tokenization, stablecoins, and Digital Asset Treasuries (DATs). Our first model connects tokenization with security design under asymmetric information. Continuous secondary-market trading generates information recovery, reducing adverse-selection costs over time and affecting both the issuance price and the optimal tokenization design. Our second model develops a dynamic corporate-finance framework for DATs, in which market valuation, capital-market financing, and crypto accumulation interact endogenously. We characterize the optimal issuance policy and illustrate the model using Strategy as a case study. A few directions for future research are discussed, providing a starting point for further theoretical and empirical study of RWA markets.

abstract: Do people behave more favorably towards their in-group during a crisis? Defining in/out-groups by geography, we study donations to local versus non-local charities during the Covid pandemic. The evidence points to increased parochialism: We document a relative increase in donations to local charities and show that donors in high-Covid areas increased their local giving and became less responsive to international disasters. Increased local giving was most pronounced during the first year of the pandemic. Our interpretation is that greater parochialism in donations was due to heightened concern about the immediate impact of Covid at a time when localities were salient.

abstract: This study develops a country-level measure of the economic-industrial capacity of European NATO Allies to mobilise, replenish, maintain, and sustain military capability under strategic stress. The measure comprises four components: macroeconomic capacity, sectoral resilience, defence-industrial capability, and logistics and sustainment. The analysis covers 28 European Allies and evaluates a balanced baseline against five geoeconomic stress scenarios. The results distinguish baseline capacity from stress vulnerability and provide an assessment framework for identifying the economic-industrial bottlenecks that can constrain sustained military readiness. Baseline scores vary materially across countries, with a sample mean of 0.610 and a range from 0.471 to 0.759. The calibrated geoeconomic shocks reduce effective capacity in every scenario, though the effects are highly heterogeneous. The combined-stress scenario has the largest average effect, lowering the sample mean to 0.491, a decline of 19.5 per cent relative to baseline. TRS and PR operate mainly through defence-industrial and replenishment constraints; supply-chain fragmentation is driven primarily by sectoral exposure and substitutability; and external-support reduction operates through allied access and sustainment. Our results suggest shifting attention from expenditure targets alone towards the capacity to convert resources into usable military capability: the key issue is not only how much is spent, but also which bottlenecks limit the conversion of resources into capability.

abstract: Childcare shortages have limited families’ access to quality care, with consequences for children’s development and parents’ careers. We link two decades of childcare supply data to longitudinal surveys of U.S. scientists. We find workplace childcare deserts are widespread: more than half of scientists at universities and research institutions work in deserts, where supply falls significantly short of demand. We further find mothers working in deserts are less likely to attain tenure. They are also more likely to move to industry and part-time positions. Reduced work time partly accounts for the tenure association but other reasons remain. Expanding childcare availability near workplaces may help retain scientific talent. The US childcare system is characterized by limited access, high costs, and uneven quality. While the COVID-19 pandemic brought the childcare crisis into sharp focus (1-4), the problem is decades old (5, 6). For years, the limited availability of affordable, high-quality childcare has strained American families (7). Yet public investment in childcare remains low relative to that of other high-income countries (8, 9). Only a handful of US states provide publicly funded preschool, and such programs primarily serve 4-year-olds only (10). For younger children, public care provision is much more limited (11), leaving families largely dependent on private providers. The labor-intensive nature of childcare, regulatory requirements, and lack of economies of scale constrain providers’ ability to expand capacity. As a result, childcare shortages are widespread (12, 13). At the same time, childcare providers often struggle financially despite low wages in the sector and high costs borne by families. Among the many challenges facing the US childcare system, limited availability is particularly consequential because families cannot use care that is simply unavailable. Before the pandemic, 73% of center-based childcare providers reported turning families away because they were full or maintaining a waiting list in 2019 (14). More recent national data also show persistent access difficulties (15). Limited access to childcare can reduce labor-force participation (9, 16, 17). Moreover, because responsibility for the care of young children continues to fall disproportionately on women (18, 19), childcare shortages may also contribute to gender disparities in education and career advancement. These constraints can be especially consequential in scientific careers. A growing literature documents associations between parenthood and researchers’ career trajectories and outcomes (20-23), yet much less is known about how the environments in which scientists work can support—or constrain—parents’ careers. Although parental leave can provide important support around childbirth (9), the demands of caregiving extend far beyond the first months of a child’s life. Because broadly available public education generally does not begin until kindergarten, families remain heavily dependent on childcare throughout children’s early years. In the absence of reliable care, researchers may leave or change professions, reduce their work activities, or reconsider family formation.

abstract: The terminal crisis of capitalism has been predicted regularly since 1848. It has not occurred. We treat this 175-year forecasting record as a stylized fact in need of a model, and we supply one. The model unifies results from five literatures: adaptive systems, mechanism design and computational complexity, behavioral decision theory, global games, and the political economy of redistribution. Ten assumptions deliver twelve formal results and one theorem. Recurring shock classes have geometrically decaying collapse hazards, and the institutional response lag within the banking class alone has fallen from 816 days (1930-33) to 18 days (2008) to 2 days (2023). A centralized replacement of the price mechanism fails on at least one of two horns, computation or truthful input, and we are explicit about which horn survives modern algorithms. Revolutionary participation requires a reference-point break, and we derive Davies's J-curve from cumulative prospect theory together with a new result: the revolutionary window closes endogenously, with length inversely proportional to the speed of hedonic adaptation, roughly four to nine years at calibrated parameters, and with its perceptibility threshold derived from the participation constraint rather than assumed. Personalized media shift protest games, in the model, into the unique no-attack equilibrium of a global game. Redistribution is a dial, not an identity: countries with nearly identical market Ginis (0.505-0.512) sustain disposable Ginis from 0.273 to 0.395. We state seven testable predictions and six falsification conditions, and we map which assumption each rival school must deny.

abstract: This study investigates the spatial relationships among housing-market appreciation, housing affordability, and automobile commuting to Toronto across 23 census metropolitan areas and municipalities in southern Ontario from 2016 to 2021. Utilizing Statistics Canada Census data, the analysis employed linear and quadratic ordinary least-squares regression, Global and Local Moran's I, and residual spatial diagnostics to assess geographic patterns in average dwelling values, owner shelter-cost burden, and lone-driver commuting. The study found that average dwelling values increased significantly throughout the region, maintaining a strong nonlinear relationship with distance from Toronto, which indicates a persistent metropolitan accessibility gradient. Commuter volumes also demonstrated pronounced nonlinear distance gradients; however, housing appreciation was not significantly correlated with percentage changes in commuting (R² = .045, p = .331), suggesting that the expansion of the housing market did not result in proportional growth in Toronto-bound automobile travel. The shelter-cost burden exhibited weaker distance relationships and greater residual spatial dependence, indicating localized affordability influences not fully explained by distance or dwelling values. Overall, the findings suggest an increasingly extensive regional housing market with spatially heterogeneous affordability and commuting outcomes, highlighting the importance of integrating housing, transportation, and regional planning.

abstract: Administrative boundary reforms in China alter the assignment of local authority and growth incentives without changing physical geography. We study two reforms with opposite institutional content-county-to-district (centralization: a county absorbed into a municipality as an urban district) and county-to-city (empowerment: a county upgraded to a county-level city)-using a firm-year pollution panel (1998-2013) and a border-pair research design that compares firms on opposite sides of the same county border. Centralizing reform lowers local NOx intensity by 14.8% through cleaner production, without shrinking output or employment; empowering reform raises COD, dust, and wastewater levels by 87-95% through dirty growth. The local abatement is not net abatement: NOx rises in same-prefecture neighbor counties (+0.77), reallocation follows administrative boundaries rather than geographic distance, is confirmed in satellite ambient data, and is not driven by wind or water transport. The reallocation operates through incumbent neighbor firms becoming dirtier, not through firm relocation or new entry. A back-of-the-envelope welfare calculation yields a statistically insignificant welfare gain from the only significant abatement (NOx, ¥47 million/yr, CI crossing zero) and a damage of-¥2.3 billion/yr from county-to-city reform. These findings show that boundary reforms reshape the spatial configuration of pollution across administrative boundaries rather than reducing it.

abstract: Pregnancy can disrupt schooling before infant care begins. We use monthly histories from the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth 1997 to study school interruptions during pregnancy and after childbirth and whether students later return to school or earn a diploma or GED. We jointly model conception and sustained interruptions in enrollment, allowing persistent unobserved differences to affect both processes. Under the timing-of-events identifying assumptions, pregnancy raises the monthly interruption rate to nearly four times the rate without pregnancy. Interruption rates are elevated before delivery and remain elevated afterward. After an interruption, students already exposed to pregnancy return to school and earn a diploma or GED less often within two years. These findings show that schooling disruption is already present during pregnancy, before the additional demands of infant care begin.

abstract: We develop a framework to compare the relative effectiveness of subsidizing alternative emission-reducing technologies. We show that an intermediate technology may reduce emissions more effectively than the cleanest technology if it induces sufficiently greater substitution away from the prevailing high-emission technology. We apply the framework to the South Korean passenger vehicle market using a demand model that incorporates mileage heterogeneity, an important determinant of fuel-type choice. First, reallocating existing subsidies from battery electric vehicles (BEVs), the cleanest technology, to hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), an intermediate technology, would reduce total greenhouse gas emissions by an additional 47%. Second, for a BEV-focused subsidy policy to outperform an HEV-focused policy, the carbon intensity of electricity generation would need to fall by approximately 45%. Our findings suggest that HEV subsidies remain more effective than BEV subsidies until consumers become sufficiently willing to switch to BEVs or electricity generation becomes sufficiently decarbonized.

abstract: Thermal noise communication systems transmit information by modulating thermal radiation, eliminating the need for a dedicated signal power source and making them attractive solutions for low-power sensor networks. Their efficiency enables long-lived, unobtrusive operation, which is valuable in the Internet of Things, electromagnetic interference-sensitive environments, and radio frequency identification tag systems. However, a limited understanding of the wireless channel model and efficient transmission schemes has hindered their practical deployment. Here, we present a wireless channel model that elucidates how systems operating at ambient temperature can modulate thermal noise to convey information. Our results reveal a thermal noise backscatter mechanism that enables significantly higher data rates than previously achieved. We designed and built a thermal noise communication system leveraging this mechanism to achieve data rates in the kilobits-per-second range—over two orders of magnitude higher than prior demonstrations. We also derive the system capacity and show that using polar codes, we are able to achieve this expected capacity. Our channel model and transmission scheme pave the way for strategies in thermal noise sensing and communication, advancing practical low-power networking for next-generation wireless applications.

abstract: How do we define an occupation? By its job title? An accountant at a small trading company keeps the books; at a listed firm the same title demands a certified-accountant licence, and the week goes to the reports that regulators and the board read. Same title, different bar, different work. What defines an occupation is who it lets in and what it asks them to do. In a rapidly changing labor market, tracking those requirements and tasks is how to take the market's pulse. Yet no instrument reads both at the speed they change. Second, counting occupations says the work most exposed to language models is disappearing, and counting tasks says far less of it is. abstract: We examine how macroeconomic and geopolitical developments in the United States, the euro area, and China affect the currency composition of central banks’ foreign exchange reserves. Using an unbalanced panel of reserve shares for 53 countries over 1999–2023, we estimate a constrained system of equations that explicitly imposes the adding-up restriction on reserve shares. The results indicate substantial persistence in reserve holdings and significant cross-currency dependence, supporting a system-wide dynamics of reserve composition. In the country fixed-effects specification (1) issuer economic size, (2) uncertainty, (3) sanctions, (4) trade linkages, and (5) issuer credibility are significantly associated with reserve allocation across currencies. With the inclusion of year fixed effects, the persistence and cross-currency dependence remain, while trade linkages and sanctions emerge as the most important determinants of reserve composition. The results highlight the importance of accounting for the compositional nature and interdependence of reserve shares when examining the determinants of global reserve holdings.

abstract: In 2019, a fire at a natural gas plant and historically low temperatures caused an emergency shortage of natural gas in Michigan. A statewide emergency text alert asked households to turn thermostats down to 65 degrees F. We analyze the effectiveness of this request using high-frequency smart-thermostat data from Michigan and four neighboring states. Using a difference-in-differences research design, we find that Michigan households reduced thermostat settings by 1.1 degrees F on average. Our results suggest that the use of the wireless emergency alert system was critical in creating an effective emergency response.  We examine heterogeneity in responsiveness by whether a household's baseline thermostat setting was above or below the compliance target of 65 degrees F and by Democratic Party gubernatorial vote share.

abstract: When robots interact with elastic surfaces such as mattresses and trampolines, changes in loading cause the surfaces to deform and rebound, altering subsequent contact locations and forces. We present Elastra, a simulation framework for modeling this interaction and supporting the training and evaluation of robot control policies. Elastra represents each surface using elements that move only vertically, with elastic connections and damping to model deformation and recovery. Contact forces drive surface motion, and the updated surface geometry is used to compute subsequent contact forces. We systematically validate our simulations against an independent implementation and a real mattress load curve. We further use Elastra to train the Unitree G1 humanoid to stand up on mattresses and trampolines. Using the pretrained HoST policy and ProtoMotions motion tracker as original controllers, we train residual policies through reinforcement learning to add corrections to their joint targets. Adding these residual policies increases the success rate with HoST from 44.1\% to 72.5\%, and from 55\% to 89\% on the trampoline. With ProtoMotions, the success rate increases from 19.0\% to 45.0\% for initial poses not encountered during training. The code and video are available on https://github.com/yichg/elastra.

abstract: Solar Radiation Management and other forms of geoengineering fundamentally invert the standard economics of climate change. Because these interventions are inexpensive and fast-acting, they replace the classic free-rider problem of global mitigation with a free-driver problem (Weitzman2015), where a single vulnerable nation can unilaterally cool the planet. We develop a macro-finance framework to formalize the asset pricing implications of this technological regime. By capping realized temperatures without reducing the atmospheric carbon stock, geoengineering acts as a put option on climate damages funded by the accumulation of "Ecological Debt." This debt introduces a catastrophic, endogenous tail risk known as a termination shock. We show that the anticipation of geoengineering initially subsidizes fossil fuel incumbents by suppressing the carbon tax, but ultimately transforms them into toxic assets as Ecological Debt deepens. Geoengineering and Carbon Dioxide Removal switch from substitutes to complements once termination risk is present.

abstract: Long-term memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to provide continuous personalized assistance by retaining user information across interactions. Existing systems support this process through fact extraction, organization, updating, and retrieval, but largely maintain memories as independent facts. This fact-centric paradigm may overlook how new facts update, constrain, or conflict with earlier ones, while leaving their applicability, role, and priority for the current request implicit. In this paper, we introduce EvoMemState, a state-centric framework that augments persistent facts with two complementary states: Relational States that capture how facts remain valid and relate to one another as memory evolves, and a Reasoning State that determines how these facts should be applied to the current request. Specifically, EvoMemState consists of three key components: (i) Ontology-Guided Memory State Induction extracts Persistent Facts and constructs Relational States that maintain their validity, scope, and evolving relations. (ii) RL-Based State Evolution internalizes memory-use experience into a policy through reinforcement learning to generate a request-specific Reasoning State. (iii) State-Aware Reasoning then combines the relevant facts with their Relational States and the generated Reasoning State to guide the personal agent. Extensive experiments on long-term dialogue and memory-use benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over existing memory systems in retrieval completeness and memory-grounded response accuracy. Our code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/XMUDeepLIT/EvoMemState.git.

abstract: This paper introduces the AI & Economy ATLAS (Activity, Task, Landscape, and Adoption Study), an ongoing economic research initiative using Google AI usage data. The first iteration of ATLAS is built on 15 million de-identified interactions across the Gemini App, Google AI Mode, and Gemini API. Using privacy-preserving algorithms as well as established and bespoke classification methods, we map AI usage to over 800 occupations, 4000 tasks, 300 household activities, 150 countries, and 140 languages. We then make a number of observations on what the data reveals about AI's diffusion, and its usage at work and in day-today life. In the workplace, we show that while AI adoption spans occupations covering just above 88% of US employment, penetration remains shallow and overwhelmingly collaborative in nature, with end-to-end task automation limited in scope. Outside of work, AI spans activities making up about 98% of Americans' non-sleep time, with disproportionately high use in high-friction tasks such as engaging with government and professional service providers, likely delivering economic value that standard national accounts may miss. Globally, adoption scales with national wealth and has broad linguistic distribution, with English queries representing only around a third of volume. As we build upon ATLAS and expand its scope and capabilities, we will continue to provide large-scale empirical evidence to inform the public, policy and academic questions about the ongoing AI transformation.

abstract: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. Recent progress in mechanistic interpretability (MI) has made it possible to identify neurons, features, circuits, population structures, and dynamical patterns associated with model behavior. As these tools improve, attention is shifting from what can be observed inside a model to how those observations support mechanistic explanations. We examine the parallel efforts of neuroscience and MI to address this question and identify recurring inferential bottlenecks when inferring mechanisms from complex neural systems. We propose five principles and organize them into a recursive logic for a more rigorous procedure of mechanistic inference. These principles provide a framework that supports scientific discovery in two senses: it helps turn local interpretability findings into cumulative knowledge of mechanisms within models, and it makes those mechanisms sufficiently precise to generate testable hypotheses about domains beyond the models. Evidence beyond MI is ultimately required to establish what model mechanisms reveal about the world.

abstract: The dispersion of self-reported life satisfaction has been proposed and used as a comprehensive measure of societal inequality. A negative cross-country association between mean life satisfaction and its standard deviation has been read as evidence that this inequality is itself welfare-relevant, but critics have pointed to the nonlinearity and boundedness of response scales. I describe a further problem: a substantial and predictable share of respondents simplify the 0–10 scale to the subset { 0 , 5 , 10 } —“focal-value rounding” ( fvr )—a behavior that breaks not only linearity of the scale but even its order, in the sense that no stretching or relabeling of response categories can undo fvr . I derive a sharp bound on the bias that fvr can induce in the standard-deviation; at empirically-typical fvr fractions the possible bias is roughly half the cross-country range of dispersion. Turning to empirical data, I estimate and correct for the bias by fitting a model of fvr behavior to the Gallup World Poll Cantril ladder (135 countries; N = 300 , 137 ) and three other multi-country life evaluations. The corrections are material: fvr inflates measured standard deviation in 133 of 135 countries, by a median of 0.090 points. However, because the corrections are nearly uniform in sign across countries, rankings of the standard deviation survive essentially intact. The ordinal inequality indices which Cowell and Flachaire advocate as the theoretically appropriate alternative suffer even worse from fvr . The correlation between mean and standard deviation survives fvr correction with modest attenuation and some caveats. Thus fvr does not, by itself, overturn previously reported correlations; it does, however, add a further reason for caution in interpreting scalar measures of subjective wellbeing inequality: candidate statistics are differently contaminated, the ordinal repairs no less than the cardinal originals, and they disagree with one another. Lastly, I show that fvr -correction can improve the pairwise dominance-comparability of full distributions.

abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an (r, Q) policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most (√ 2 + √ 6)/2 < 1.932 times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor √ 2 relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic 1.79 upper guarantee to a uniform √ 2 guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about 1.59 for our heuristic (r, Q) policy and 1.47 after joint optimization of r and Q. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from 2.33% to 3.91%, depending on the setup cost.

abstract: Generative artificial intelligence illustrates a broader organizational puzzle: young, resourceconstrained firms can build on knowledge produced across a wider field to address problems that exceed their internal experience. We theorize one mechanism as social imitation: a distributed and recursive process through which communities observe practices and outcomes across organizations, distill recurrent elements into portable strategies, circulate them, and revise the collective repertoire as adoption produces new evidence. This perspective endogenizes the object of imitation. Organizations do not merely copy practices; communities collectively produce what becomes available to copy. We distinguish the source of a candidate-directly observed organizations or a collective-from its mode of adoption-blind or informed-and examine four forms of imitation in an agent-based model of organizational search. Collective sourcing alone does not improve performance. Its value depends on situated evaluation: assessing whether a candidate fits the adopter's configuration. As interdependence increases, informed social imitation improves population performance and the best solution discovered. As problems grow, it becomes more likely to outperform informed imitation from one or several directly observed peers because collective distillation sustains a broader candidate repertoire. Most gains arise from evaluating a small candidate set, and population performance can improve when only a minority of organizations possesses evaluative capability. Social imitation thus reveals a division of cognitive labor: communities expand the strategies organizations can consider, while organizations create value by determining which strategies fit. It explains how firms can mobilize knowledge beyond their boundaries-and why widespread access to collective knowledge does not produce equal benefits.

abstract: Academic journals are part of the infrastructure of science, yet most journal titles are owned by commercial publishers while their standing rests on editors and boards who can leave. This paper asks what that separation means for the governance of science. Using a coded dataset of all 57 editorial mass resignations recorded by Retraction Watch from 2015 to 2026, data on editor tenure at 110 economics, finance and accounting journals, and journal-level publication and revenue data, I document three patterns. First, resignation does not reverse an owner’s decision: in none of the 19 episodes involving an editor’s replacement did the owner back down after the board resigned, so editorial communities have influence only before they leave. Second, whether a departing board can take a journal’s standing with it depends on institutions outside the board: successor journals follow most often where a scholarly society backs the board and rarely in medicine, where non-profit hosts are scarce, while journal ranking lists, which rate titles rather than the people who edit them, keep reputation with the owner. Third, a stated limit on editor tenure was applied at the publisher’s discretion; where it was applied, output grew almost fourfold, a short-run gain whose long-run effect on the journal’s standing is not yet known. I draw implications for scholarly societies, funders, publishers, and the bodies that compile journal rankings.

abstract: Many heritage institutions hold extensive collections of show programs. Too numerous to be cataloged individually, they remain difficult to access and are still largely undigitized. This paper presents a workflow for transforming such documents into structured, interoperable data by combining vision-language models (VLMs), a custom extension of the Linked Art ontology for the performing arts, and different approaches for automatic semantic data annotation. Using the Festival d’Avignon programs (1947–present), preserved at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, as a case study, we demonstrate how VLMs achieve more than 98% text transcription accuracy from heterogeneous heritage document images and how constraining large language model generation through a knowledge graph significantly reduces hallucinations in semantic annotation. We argue that this workflow opens new possibilities for large-scale, interoperable performing arts historiography, including the creation of catalogues raisonnés for performing artists, a form of scholarship common in visual arts but absent in performing arts studies.

abstract: A legged robot can learn to walk inside a learned simulator: a neural network that predicts the robot's next state and is run forward on its own predictions. They are usually trained and checked one step ahead, although a policy uses them for a hundred steps or more. We audit one published system end to end, without a GPU: the dynamics model of the Robotic World Model (RWM) for the ANYmal D quadruped, and the uncertainty estimate of its follow-up, RWM-U. We rebuilt the model to match the released code's outputs, losses and gradients exactly, measured 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies and 38 simulators of three other architectures, and trained policies inside simulators that we tested in a hand-built MuJoCo model of the robot. Training on the model's own rollouts beat one-step training at 368 steps on all ten held-out episodes (registered), although one-step training was better one step ahead. One-step checks therefore misjudge design choices: pruning 30% of the weights kept 90% of the model's skill one step ahead and 39% at 2 s. Ensemble disagreement ranked rollout error well (Spearman +0.90 at 100 steps), yet covered 4.6% of outcomes at one sigma, against 68% for a calibrated estimate, as each network's own variance collapses under the implemented loss. Two checks that need no recorded future ranked some pools of simulators well, but neither was shown better than 8-step error in a primary test. At the robot level, accuracy has not predicted walking: all 18 fine-tuned copies we tested predicted better than the released model one and eight steps ahead, yet 13 gave failing policies, and registered tests of whether any check ranks simulators by their policies were not settled. In a secondary test, running the authors' policy inside each simulator ranked them well. We also report nine of our own claims that we withdrew. Scope: one robot, one gait, simulated data, no hardware.

Ensemble disagreement ranked rollout error well (Spearman +0.90 at 100 steps), yet covered 4.6% of outcomes at one sigma, against 68% for a calibrated estimate, as each network's own variance collapses under the implemented loss. Two checks that need no recorded future ranked some pools of simulators well, but neither was shown better than 8-step error in a primary test. abstract: Identifying time preference shocks is challenging: shocks large enough to shift survey-elicited stated impatience also tighten financial resources, confounding the interpretation of stated time preference. Jointly examining stated and revealed preferences resolves this identification problem: impatience shocks and reductions in financial resources generate opposite consumption responses, even though both raise stated impatience. Applying our identification framework to the 2009 L'Aquila earthquake, we combine panel data with spatially granular seismic and damage data in a difference-indifferences design that compares undamaged households that experienced the earthquake with a spatial control group at similar distances from the epicenter. Treated households report greater impatience and increase nondurable consumption by 11 percent relative to controls. Effects are consistent with a psychological-stress channel, concentrated among the most vulnerable to stress, and persist as households deplete their liquid wealth buffer over time.

abstract: Abstract This paper proposes an unsupervised workflow to pseudo-label extracellular spikes from human brain slice MEA recordings into two putative cell types: pyramidal cells and interneurons. Here, the raw data from the data acquisition system is used and processed. The pipeline for preprocessing includes bandpass filtering, threshold-based spike detection, frame alignment and normalization. In the ML workflow, dimensionality reduction (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP), clustering (GMM, k-means). To achieve an online system, template matching and OSort under varying curation strictness is also considered. All pipelines are evaluated by different cluster quality with within-cluster Pearson correlation, Silhouette score, and Calinski-Harabasz index. Applying stricter curation improves separation at some cost to inclusivity.

abstract: Data-driven sequential decision making in marketing and healthcare can benefit from observations collected in related environments, particularly when data in the environment of interest are limited. Transferring such information requires accounting for differences in rewards and transition dynamics across environments. We study knowledge transfer for offline reinforcement learning through a joint estimation framework that directly integrates source information into target value-function learning. We propose Direct Transfer Fitted Q-Iteration (DFQI), which updates the target Q-function while simultaneously borrowing the source information through an L1 penalty that links the target coefficients to a weighted aggregate of source coefficients, with both determined jointly within each Bellman update. Using sieve approximation, we establish statistical guarantees for target estimation and policy learning in stationary discounted environments with common or heterogeneous transition kernels. Empirical studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed DFQI framework in transferring source information to improve policy learning with limited target data.

abstract: Abstract The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.

abstract: Research activity generates highly localized positive spillovers, yet in the U.S. it has become increasingly spatially misaligned with population and economic activity as people moved away from legacy cities where major research institutions remain anchored. Reallocating researchers toward population centers could broaden local access to knowledge but may reduce knowledge production if legacy institutions or large research clusters raise researcher output. The spatial reallocation of researchers therefore entails a trade-off between gains in knowledge access and losses in knowledge production. To quantify the knowledge production loss from reallocation, we use bibliographic data to separate individual effects from location effects and show that location effects account for substantial differences in research output across locations. Our instrumental-variables estimates provide robust evidence of own-institution agglomeration effects but weaker evidence of external-cluster effects. We then incorporate these estimates into counterfactual reallocations and show that marginally reallocating researchers toward large metropolitan areas with relatively little research activity can plausibly raise aggregate output because the associated knowledge production losses are modest and can be offset by small access gains.
